items.stem: An organization needs to validate its disaster recovery plan without disrupting production. Which Azure Site Recovery capability should it use?

options.rationale: Correct: test failover runs the recovery in an isolated network without affecting the production workload.
Unplanned failover switches production to the secondary site and is for real outages.
Deleting the vault removes replication configuration; it does not test recovery.
Disabling replication stops protection and tests nothing.

items.explanation: Correct: test failover runs the recovery in an isolated network without affecting the production workload.

items.stem: A workload must recover with no more than 30 seconds of data loss. Which objective does this define?

options.rationale: Correct: RPO defines the maximum acceptable data loss, measured as time.
RTO defines how long recovery may take, not how much data may be lost.
SLA credits are financial remedies, not recovery objectives.
MTBF is a reliability metric, not a recovery objective.

items.explanation: Correct: RPO defines the maximum acceptable data loss, measured as time.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Azure Backup and Azure Site Recovery are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Site Recovery replicates and fails over running workloads
options.rationale: Correct: Site Recovery keeps apps running by replicating to a secondary location and failing over.

options.text: Azure Backup keeps recoverable copies of data
options.rationale: Correct: Azure Backup protects data by keeping recoverable copies.

options.text: Site Recovery removes the need for any backups
options.rationale: DR replication and backup serve different purposes and are complementary.

options.text: Azure Backup orchestrates multi-tier application failover
options.rationale: Orchestrated failover of multi-tier apps is a Site Recovery recovery-plan feature.

items.explanation: Correct: Site Recovery keeps apps running by replicating to a secondary location and failing over.
